summary: Changes the schedule for moving from the old Telnet to the new one, after worries about a coordinated switch. New Telnet implementations were still to be ready on 1 January 1974 but were to use ICP socket 23.

eli5.summary: Switching everyone to the new remote-login system on one day was too hard. The plan was relaxed so the new one ran at its own address.

subtitle: A revised schedule for switching to a new version of the remote-login protocol.

tldr.problem: Early plans to switch the entire network from old Telnet to new Telnet on a single date risked disrupting services because of potential incompatibilities between versions.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC relaxes the switchover: new Telnet implementations listen on socket 23 (the standard port), allowing old and new versions to coexist. FTP socket 21 is left unchanged until a separate switchover is coordinated.
tldr.outcome: The more gradual transition allowed testing and debugging without service disruption, and socket 23 became the permanent standard port for Telnet.

today: RFC 593 set the stage for modern Telnet, which has used port 23 since this transition. The protocol itself was later made historic as more secure alternatives like SSH replaced it.

sections.title: The Telnet Transition Problem
sections.content:
By late 1973, the ARPANET was preparing a major upgrade to the Telnet protocol, the tool for remote login across the network. A coordinated switchover date had been set, but implementers and users worried about incompatibilities that could break services if the transition was too abrupt.

RFC 593 announces a revised schedule that allows the new and old Telnet systems to coexist during a transition period.
sections.eli5: A new remote-login system was ready, but forcing everyone to switch the same day could break things. Instead, both versions could run side by side.

sections.title: The New Arrangement
sections.content:
New Telnet implementations were still due by 1 January 1974, but instead of replacing the old system immediately, they would use ICP socket 23 (the decimal port number). This allowed the old Telnet to keep running on its original socket while new implementations listened on socket 23.

User Telnet programs could optionally select which socket to connect to, and some implementations (like MIT-DMCG) were dual-stack—able to handle both old and new protocols—enabling testing without disruption.
sections.eli5: The new Telnet would listen at address 23, the old one at its old address. Systems could try the new one when they were ready.

sections.title: FTP and Follow-up
sections.content:
The RFC also adjusts the File Transfer Protocol schedule: new FTP implementations were due by 1 February 1974 but would continue using ICP socket 21 until a separate switchover decision could be made.

During January 1974, the network liaisons would survey the status of implementations and determine when a full switchover could happen without disrupting service.
sections.eli5: File transfer got the same deal: the new version could be ready, but the old address stayed in use until everyone was confident.
